minutes.headline: Committee voted to recommend DiGiorgio Associates as architect for the Town Hall project after scoring three firms.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed reference checks on three architect finalists and scored each against the RFQ rubric. It also heard from a facilities official about asbestos and hazardous materials testing in the building. It then voted to recommend DiGiorgio Associates, and discussed warrant placeholders, a press release and meeting dates.

what_happened.line: The Building Design Committee voted to recommend DiGiorgio Associates as architect for the Town Hall project.
Before the vote, the committee scored the three finalist firms against the RFQ rubric after hearing reference check reports.
A facilities official briefed the committee on asbestos and hazardous materials testing in the building.
The committee agreed to put placeholder articles on the next agenda so they reach the Town Meeting warrant before it closes.
The committee set meetings for the 19th and 26th at 6 pm, dropping the twelfth, and planned a press release once the contract is signed.

why_it_matters: The choice of architect begins the design work on the Town Hall project, and the warrant placeholders are how funding for it could reach a Town Meeting vote that residents are asked to take.
Hazardous material testing in the building bears on the eventual project cost, which would fall mostly on taxes.
watch_next: The next committee agenda, which is to include the Town Meeting warrant placeholder articles before the warrant closes.
Signing of the architect contract, after which a press release and community outreach item are planned.
